card.name: Dose-adjustment verbs after 'may'
card.fires_on: The small word right after 'dosage/dose may' or 'should' (mostly 'be', sometimes 'if' or 'increased') in dosing instructions about raising or adjusting a dose.

modes.label: 'be' after may
modes.description: The word 'be' following 'dose/dosage may', leading into 'increased' or 'used'.
modes.example: The dosage may<< be>> increased at weekly (or longer) intervals

modes.label: Increase wording
modes.description: The verb 'increased' after 'should be' or 'gradually' when a dose is titrated upward.
modes.example: This may be gradually<< increased>> if needed and tolerated [see Use in

modes.label: 'if' after increases
modes.description: The word 'if' after 'Increases may be made', before 'indicated'.
modes.example: Increases may be made<< if>> indicated. Dosage should not exceed
